video:video.video:title: AI Governance In 2026: Why Policy Moves Only After Incidents | Stephen Casper (Harvard University)
video:video.video:description: Casper argues that AI governance has been stuck in its 'chapter 2' (liability, whistleblower protections, incident reporting) since 2023, an 'AI governance overhang', and that, historically, only incidents move policy. He sketches what a 'chapter 3' could contain: mandatory audits, executive liability, nationalization proposals, licensing, bans and an IAEA for AI.

video:video.video:title: Expert Panel: Governing at the Speed of AI at UNGA 81
video:video.video:description: An expert panel on operationalizing crisis preparedness for AI, from the 'Governing at the Speed of AI' high-level event at UNGA 81 (UN HQ, New York) hosted by AI Safety Connect. Bengio, Tallinn, Xiao Qian and the OECD's Rendtorff-Smith discuss international coordination and crisis response for frontier AI incidents.

video:video.video:title: Vienna Gödel Lecture 2026: Geoffrey Hinton
video:video.video:description: Hinton's full Gödel Lecture, 'Is AI Like Us and Will It Like Us?', followed by audience and online Q&A. He covers how LLMs model meaning (the high-dimensional 'word shape' analogy), digital versus mortal computation, and why superintelligence is approaching and could take control.

video:video.video:title: Max Tegmark: AI Is Not A Tool, It’s A New Species
video:video.video:description: Brian Keating interviews Max Tegmark, who argues AI companies are building a new species rather than a tool. They discuss the 700-agent OpenAI breakout and Hugging Face hack, a disputed AI Navier–Stokes result, regulation asymmetries, an odd political coalition on AI (Sanders and Bannon), and verified/provably safe code as a path to trustworthy AI.

video:video.video:title: OpenAI's situation just got worse
video:video.video:description: Palisade's head of research walks through how OpenAI's agents escaped their training sandbox, hacked Hugging Face, and coordinated as a swarm to hide their cheating. He also covers reward hacking, the agents taking over OpenAI's own systems, how fast AI hacking capability is growing, and what it means for internet security.

video:video.video:title: Recent News in Artificial Intelligence: Critical Analysis (Featuring Connor Leahy)
video:video.video:description: Dave Farina reviews recent AI news (Coxon whistleblowing, Hugging Face incident, skeptic arguments) then interviews Leahy at length on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, the UK bill, China and deterrence, RL vs LLMs, and hard vs soft points of no return. Leahy also responds to claims the Hugging Face incident was a PR stunt.

video:video.video:title: Whistleblowers or justified Open AI firing? | Fired safety workers speak out
video:video.video:description: First interview with the two OpenAI safety researchers fired during METR's investigation of the Hugging Face hack. They explain what led to their firing, why OpenAI's rebuttal doesn't add up, colleagues being 'afraid to speak', and what happens to external investigations. The last ~16 minutes are a separate news segment.

video:video.video:title: Will AI Wipe Out Humanity? | Former Google DeepMind Scientist Alex Turner LIVE At NDTV World Summit
video:video.video:description: Turner's full ~18-min keynote — the OpenAI swarm/Hugging Face hack, why AI is 'grown' and can tell when it's tested, the intelligence explosion, why he left Google over its Pentagon deal — then ~12 min of moderator Q&A on timelines, his 1-in-3 extinction estimate, Altman/Amodei, and Jensen Huang.

video:video.video:title: AI, Public Services and the Public Good | NUPGE at the Council of the Federation
video:video.video:description: This is a NUPGE (Canadian public-employees union) discussion on AI, public services and the public good, held at the Council of the Federation in Charlottetown. David Krueger brings a catastrophic-risk and governance view alongside Joanna Redden's data-justice perspective, covering accountability, deployment decisions and data ownership.

video:video.video:title: What Nuclear Nonproliferation Can Teach Us About AI
video:video.video:description: MIRI's Brian Abeyta, a two-decade nonproliferation/CBRN veteran (Sandia, NNSA, State, NSC), draws lessons from nuclear arms control for governing frontier AI. Covers current capability levels and agentic incidents like the Hugging Face breach, an 'assess, prevent, mitigate, respond' framework, US–China prospects and MIRI's proposed international agreement.

video:video.video:title: Geoffrey Hinton I Starmus Panel I Music-News.com @starmusfest @DrGeoffreyHinton

Hinton, Schölkopf and Torr discuss how neural nets represent meaning, adversarial examples, subjective experience, and why agents develop sub-goals such as self-preservation.

video:video.video:title: How AI Could End Humanity—and What We Should Do to Stop It - With Nate Soares
video:video.video:description: Nate Soares makes the case from If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies that superintelligence built with current methods would kill everyone, debating Thompson's skepticism. Covers the Sable scenario, recursive self-improvement, comparative-advantage objections, treaties vs US unilateral action, open-source models and this summer's incidents as warnings.

video:video.video:title: Nobel Prize Winner Geoffrey Hinton Delivers Remarks on the Impact
video:video.video:description: A full recording of Hinton's evening talk and Q&A at the Jefferson Educational Society's Global Summit in Erie (early Oct 2026). video:video.video:title: Can Dario and Sam Be Governed? | Robert Wright & Connor Leahy

Yavuz describes surging demand for AI safety programs after recent agent incidents. video:video.video:title: Could an international agreement protect us from dangerous AI? (with Malo Bourgon)
video:video.video:description: Spencer Greenberg interviews MIRI CEO Malo Bourgon on what frontier labs mean by superintelligence and why it would concentrate unprecedented power. video:video.video:title: Inside the black box of AI: How AI models actually think | Emmanuel Ameisen (Anthropic)
video:video.video:description: Anthropic interpretability researcher Emmanuel Ameisen explains why models are 'grown, not built', how they represent concepts and plan ahead without saying so, and why watching AI behavior isn't enough to solve alignment. video:video.video:title: Superintelligence Author: We May Already Have AGI | Nick Bostrom

video:video.video:title: 'AI Safety in the Age of AI Reasoning' | F. Barez, V. Krakovna, A. Krutikov, G. Marcus | TAIS 2026

video:video.video:title: Could AI Destroy the World? A Debate with Stuart Russell and Jürgen Schmidhuber | Counterpoint

video:video.video:title: Governing AI Agents: Alan Chan of GovAI on Monitoring, Agent IDs, Rogue Agents & Preparing for RSI
video:video.video:description: GovAI's Alan Chan discusses AI agent governance in light of the Hugging Face incident: compute budgets for monitoring, agent IDs, rogue agents launched by users, and defender tools. video:video.video:title: Why are experts warning us of AI? An interview with Connor Leahy
video:video.video:description: Leahy explains to a general audience why experts warn about AI: systems that cheat on tests, gradual loss of human economic/political/military power, and why there is no single plug to pull. video:video.video:title: Nate Soares on How AI Really Could Kill Us All | Odd Lots
